qc_b_main_wall_2.blurb: The tallest and busiest face at Mont Wright, a small hill just outside Quebec City near Stoneham. Twenty-six climbs split between traditional lines, top-rope problems and a handful of bolted routes, with one aid line. Difficulty runs from easy 5.6 and 5.7 up through the 5.9 and 5.10 range, with a solid block of 5.11 and 5.12 for stronger climbers. Plenty of gentle routes make it a practical pick for families, newer leaders and instruction days. Bring a harness and your own anchor kit for setting up top ropes; the walk in is short but steep and rough, and the upper section is aided by fixed cables and ladders.
qc_b_main_wall_2.approach: From the lot, follow the main trail uphill; signposts lead to the Grand Mur. The path is short but steep and rough.

qc_amphith_tre.blurb: The largest of the six cliffs in the Laurentians climbing park near Saint-Adolphe-d'Howard and Sainte-Agathe, about an hour from Montreal. Around two dozen routes share the face, a bit more bolted than traditional, and you can walk around to the top to rig top ropes. Grades start at easy 5.5, cluster in the 5.7 to 5.8 range, and thin out toward a single 5.11, so the wall suits newer climbers and those building up mileage as well as intermediates looking for a mix of protection styles. Most of the park's cliffs are only a short walk from the car.
